title: Graceful-fallback infographics and annotated debug screenshots for retry/backoff and timeout troubleshooting
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a suite of lightweight infographics and annotated product screenshots for the onboarding/quickstart docs that explain graceful fallbacks, retry/backoff strategies, and timeout diagnostics. Assets should be usable in the public docs, in-product help overlays, and a short ‘Troubleshooting for Engineers’ PDF. Focus: clear sequencing of user-visible outcomes (rate limit -> exponential backoff -> fallback model), how to read the Console traces for latency vs token errors, and specific copy for SDK-level retries and headers to inspect.
acceptance_criteria: Three infographic variants exported (hero 1200px, card 600px, narrow 420px) in SVG and PNG
Annotated product screenshots with callouts for Console trace, request headers, and SDK retry logs (3 examples: rate-limit, timeout, kv-cache-miss)
Finalized microcopy approved by PM and Eng and included in quickstart docs PR
WCAG AA contrast checks for text overlays passed
Design handoff notes + tokenized assets added to Figma file and linked in this ticket
Docs PR created that embeds hero infographic and the three annotated screenshots
assets_needed: High-fidelity Console screenshots from Staging account (region: us-west-2)
Live SDK logs snippet (anonymized) for retry sequence
Brand-approved illustration set (icon pack) for backoff, clock, shield, fallback model

decisions: Use linear timeline layout rather than flowchart: reviewers preferred stepwise UX for quick comprehension
Prefer SVG for hero to maintain crispness across docs and console; also export raster sizes for email and in-app cards
Do not show raw request IDs in screenshots; will show redacted placeholders and callout the header key to inspect
Include a short code snippet showing recommended client-side backoff (exponential with jitter) rather than pseudo-code copy
tradeoffs: Using real screenshots improves credibility but requires extra sanitization steps and may delay delivery (tradeoff: accuracy vs speed)
Simplifying the sequence to three steps (detect -> backoff -> fallback) keeps onboarding focused but omits rarer fallback routes (manual retry queues)
Accessibility constraints required higher contrast which reduced color palette nuance for the illustrations

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Leaking PII or request IDs in screenshots. Mitigation: ENG-run sanitization script and manual review before export (PR linked).
Risk: Runtime engineers request additional technical depth that bloats the asset. Mitigation: keep primary asset high-level and link to a technical appendix in docs for advanced debugging.
Risk: Assets look different in Console dark mode. Mitigation: provide both light and dark variants and test in staging console theme toggles.
